text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:
-Experts believe that exploration off mid-Norway due to start at the end of March may uncover major oil reserves.

-The ruling Labour Party wants supermarkets and grocery stores to close at 9 p.m. at the latest on weekdays and 6 p.m. at the latest on Saturdays. Kiosks would be allowed to stay open longer provided they are not too big.
-King Harald and Queen Sonja will attend a banquet in April which will commemorate the 50th anniversary of the Kon Tiki expedition.
-Kvaerner wins major contract to build production ship for the North Sea Jotun oil field.
-Rosenborg will meet Juventus in Wednesday's European Cup quarter-final second-leg match. Juventus think they will win, but Rosenborg have nothing to lose.
-Houston-based Transocean Offshore has announced it will spin off some non-core assets within its drilling services line of business in Norway.
- Kvaerner Construction in Tampa, Florida, will build schools in the United States in three projects worth 450 million crowns.
-The OECD says Norway's economy is operating near capacity and a tight monetary policy is necessary to keep it from overheating.
